chunks: Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“When you reach al-‘Aqīq from the direction of Iraq, or a miqāt from these mawāqīt, while intending ihram, if Allah wills, then remove the hair from your underarms, trim your nails, apply depilatory to your pubic area, and take from your mustache. It does not harm you whichever of that you begin with. Then use the siwāk, perform ghusl, and wear your two garments. Let your completion of that, if Allah the Exalted wills, be at the sun’s decline; and if that is not at the sun’s decline, then there is no harm, except that this is more beloved to me: that it be at the sun’s decline.”

key_terms.إِبْطَيْكَ: your underarms, whose hair is to be removed
key_terms.اسْتَكْ: use the siwāk to clean the teeth
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامَ: the sacred state entered for hajj or ‘umrah
key_terms.الْعَقِيقِ: al-‘Aqīq, a miqat for those coming from Iraq
key_terms.الْمَوَاقِيتِ: the designated stations for entering ihram
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s decline from its zenith, i.e. midday
key_terms.عَانَتَكَ: your pubic area, to be cleaned with depilatory

ai.seo_question: What preparations should be done before entering ihram at the miqat?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the recommended preparations before entering ihram at the miqat, including bodily grooming, siwak, ghusl, and putting on the two garments. It also indicates that completing these preparations around midday is preferred, though delaying beyond that time is permissible.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2533 - Mu‘awiyah ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"When you reach Al-‘Aqiq coming from Iraq, or any of the designated miqats (stations for Ihram), and you intend to enter Ihram, if Allah (swt) wills, then remove the hair from your underarms, trim your nails, clean your private area, and trim your mustache. It does not matter in which order you begin these actions. Then use the siwak (tooth-stick), take a ritual bath (ghusl), and wear your two garments for Ihram. Let this preparation, if Allah (swt) wills, be completed by the time of midday (zawal).
If it is not completed by midday, there is no harm, but it is more beloved to me that it coincides with midday."
